scope.population: the row counts of the three markout slices named in inputs, plus one re-parsed day compared against the stored slice of it
scope.window: the span each slice carries; the determinism leg re-parses one day of it
scope.coins: every coin present in the slices; the counts are compared per coin and are not restricted to one

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

checks.name: determinism_reparse
checks.assumption: re-walking December day 20251204 / BTC through the ORIGINAL build_quickwin_markouts.parse_day reproduces the stored npz slice (row count + WHOLE-ROW joint multiset of the load-bearing columns)
checks.method: bq.parse_day -> bq.compute_markouts_all, then compare (1) row count and (2) the JOINT-TUPLE multiset over the load-bearing columns (entry_px, mo1/mo10/mo60, start_pos, taker_side): both sides are lexsorted by the SAME tolerance-quantized key over ALL columns and compared ROW-BY-ROW, so cross-column row-pairing is preserved and a row-assembly scramble cannot pass; rows are NOT keyed by taker_id (global in the npz, local on a standalone re-parse)
checks.note: re-parse reproduced the stored day/coin slice exactly: identical row count and an identical WHOLE-ROW joint multiset over every load-bearing column (NaN counts match) -> the stored npz IS a deterministic product of parse_day
